case_distinctions.distinct: Existing identity coverage addresses class/script/binding separation and facet display identity. It never directly asserts valid namespace idFromString readdressing of durable state. No separate credit is assigned to same-name equality or getByName alone.

Exercises actual newUniqueId address creation and later valid string reopening, rather than a named ID, a supplied facet display ID or a changed namespace. Two samples are a finite identity check, not randomness/entropy/statistical collision certification.
One compound byte-boundary/full-name contract. Cases are not split by length, suffix or Unicode parameter values. No malformed names, truncated IDs or cryptographic validation failures are submitted.

Constructor readiness gates the very first event plus a newly arriving event. This is ordinary public initialization, with no nested blocks, competing gate owners, stale continuations, reset, timer failure, runtime fault or native-state seam.

This is an already-live object and ordinary per-request block rather than constructor readiness or storage.transaction. The second same-class root directly distinguishes root-local admission from class-global blocking. No native gate contention, reentry or failure scenario is recreated.

excluded_without_case_ids: Same name/class identity alone: subsumed by preserved duplicate-names and U014/U015/U017.
Facet display-kind/name inheritance: Z201/Z202 already covers it.
Static/dynamic module namespace: M008 is an ECMAScript module identity test, not a DO ID helper test.
Lazy get-only object activation: omitted because an independent nonactivation witness would add more machinery than coverage.
Nested/contended blocks, stale drivers and failure/reset/timeout handling: excluded guarded-core territory, no rephrased case.
Separate name lengths, character alphabets, unique ID counts or routing ingress permutations: no distinct credit.
prohibited_scope: No N001-N036 retry or reproduction, G/N/P/J122 native paths, invalid/foreign/forged IDs, auth/HMAC-failure tests, lease/draining, ownership takeover, fault injection, retained stateless capabilities or malformed input.

oracle_review_notes.resolution: Removed the incidental assertion that first/shortcut/parsed accesses all preserve the same server ctx.id.name. Official ID docs describe name omission on idFromString access; how that per-access wording applies to reuse of an already initialized live state.id remains ambiguous. State/identity continuity is still the primary contract. No name-retention compatibility or separate metadata-case credit is claimed.

Corrected client stub.name to retain full supplied names under the official Stub contract; the server ctx.id.name byte cutoff remains. Source-predicted compatibility failure is labeled separately from UNRUN.

count_rationale: Five distinct contracts survive overlap/scope review; no padding to the suggested six-to-twelve size.
